details:
INDUSPULSE — Interactive NISAR Radar Data Explorer

INDUSPULSE is an interactive geospatial visualization platform developed by Team Orbital Intelligence for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. The project focuses on the Lower Indus Basin in Sindh, Pakistan, and uses NASA-ISRO NISAR Level-2 Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance (GCOV) radar data.

The platform transforms complex satellite radar information into an accessible web-based mapping experience. It presents four raster visualization layers: HHHH, HVHV, Polarization Ratio (PR), and Polarization Ratio in decibels (PR_dB). Users can interact with the map, switch between layers, adjust visualization opacity, explore geographic coordinates, and access methodology and data-lineage information.

INDUSPULSE is developed using React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL JS, and Supabase Storage. Its reported data workflow involves intermediate GeoTIFF raster layers, derived polarization-ratio layers, and PNG map tiles hosted through Supabase for interactive visualization.

The project aims to make NISAR radar information easier to explore for students, researchers, and Earth science enthusiasts, particularly in regions where satellite-based environmental observation is valuable.

Project Goal: To bridge the gap between complex satellite radar datasets and accessible geospatial exploration through an interactive, user-friendly platform.

Live Application: https://nasa-space-app-challenge-2026-pi.vercel.app/
